question: How closely do Binance USD-M and Hyperliquid native funding payments agree over their common history after both are represented as funding paid within the same UTC eight-hour clock blocks?

sources.binance: official public USD-M monthly fundingRate archives

alignment.binning: floor each event timestamp to its UTC eight-hour block
alignment.primary_block_rate: arithmetic sum of all venue funding rates observed inside the block
alignment.secondary_block_rate: compound product of (1 + event rate) minus 1
alignment.paired_sample: intersection of blocks with at least one event from both venues

required_statistics: first and last event and block by venue and asset
event count and paired block count
Pearson and Spearman correlation of additive eight-hour rates
sign agreement including positive, negative and zero categories
Hyperliquid event-count distribution per eight-hour block
sensitivity comparison between additive and compounded block rates

acceptable_as_level_proxy_if: paired coverage is sufficiently broad and explicitly reported
sign agreement and correlation are not structurally unstable across assets and years
mean bias is not so large that Binance level costs would systematically misstate Hyperliquid costs
proxy_gate.otherwise: Binance may be used only for stress bounds or directional context, not as a point estimate for Hyperliquid funding PNL

prohibited: no calibration coefficient fitted to maximize PNL
no omission of weak assets or years
no post-result alignment change under this audit ID
next_experiment_rule: A frozen-holdings funding attribution may proceed only after this audit classifies whether Binance is a level proxy, a sign/regime proxy, or merely an external stress source for Hyperliquid.
